title: Register Convention: The Credit Standing on a Registration from Which Something Has Been Spent
content:
Where a spend already stands among a registration's entries, the credit standing used to fix the least the customer must spend under the Belrose Trade-In and Upgrade Programmes is read as this convention directs, and the reading depends on whether the programme allows its credit to be spent in parts.

## The convention

Where a spend stands among the registration's entries and the programme allows the credit to be spent in parts, the credit standing is read as the sum of every entry booked to the registration that moves the credit, spends included. Where a spend stands among those entries and the programme does not allow the credit to be spent in parts, the credit standing is read as the credit the registration shows as issued. Where no spend stands among the entries, no special reading applies.

An entry moves the credit where it books the credit, revalues it upward, spends it or takes it away; a valuation entry and an inspection entry move nothing, whatever amount they carry. A spend or a forfeit carries a negative amount.

## Whether the programme allows part-spending

| Programme | Credit may be spent in parts |
|---|---|
| Belrose Standard Trade-In | no |
| Diamond Trade-Up Guarantee | no |
| Bridal Upgrade Guarantee | yes |
| Lifetime Diamond Upgrade Guarantee | yes |
| Signature Collection Upgrade Privilege | yes |
| Estate Purchase and Consignment Programme | yes |

## Hypothetical example

A registration shows 6000 USD issued and carries a credit entry of 6000 USD, a revaluation of 400 USD, a spend of 1000 USD and a valuation entry of 7500 USD.

- Under the Bridal Upgrade Guarantee, which allows part-spending: the credit standing is 6000 plus 400 less 1000, which is 5400 USD; the valuation entry counts for nothing.
- Under the Diamond Trade-Up Guarantee, which does not: the credit standing is the 6000 USD the registration shows as issued.
